clue.text: Astronaut has room to work

parts.note: room in the sense of free area or capacity is space
to man a station or machine is to work it

explanation.surface: A spacefarer is given a cabin in which to carry out duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' looks like part of the room's purpose, but it is a verb: to man something is to operate it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who travels beyond Earth's atmosphere is an astronaut, informally a man of space.

clue.text: Dimensions of fish plates!

explanation.surface: A question about how big the plates of a fish are.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about fish sizes, but it splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Scales are relative sizes or proportions, as in a map's ratio; scales are also the small bony plates that cover a fish.

clue.text: Stir and almost take wash

indicators.note: take means the shortened word holds the next piece inside it
almost means the word and loses its final letter, stopping just short

parts.note: a wash is the disturbed water left behind a boat, its wake

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a little and then has a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter of 'and', and 'take' sets the wake inside what remains. 'wash' looks like cleaning, but it is the trail of water behind a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone from sleep is to rouse them, a synonym.

clue.text: Rat at heart, Eric is inconsistent

indicators.note: at heart means the word rat sits in the middle of the name that follows

explanation.surface: A man called Eric is fickle because he is a rat at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconsistent is irregular and unpredictable, a synonym.

clue.text: Option to convert indigene

parts.note: to convert something is to alter or change it
an indigene is a person born in a place, a native

explanation.surface: A choice offered to change a local person's beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convert' suggests religious conversion, but it simply means change.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is a choice among possibilities, a synonym.

clue.text: Take to be play about mushroom

indicators.note: about means the word for play goes around the next piece

parts.note: to play a role is to act
a cep is an edible wild mushroom, the porcino

explanation.surface: Something is supposed to be a drama about a fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something to be true is to believe it, a synonym.

clue.text: Scottish devil can start game of cards wearing cravate

indicators.note: start means only the opening letter of the word can is used

parts.note: loo is an old card game
a cravat or cravate is a neckcloth, a tie, and wearing one puts it on the card game

explanation.surface: A Scottish fiend may begin a card game while dressed in a neckcloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes C from 'can'. Loo is a crossword staple for an old card game, not a toilet here.
explanation.definitionFit: Clootie is a Scots name for the Devil, from cloot, a cloven hoof.

clue.text: Drill duty to protect the queen!

indicators.note: to protect means the duty word wraps around the royal abbreviation

parts.note: excise is a tax or duty on goods
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A soldier's drill is a duty that guards the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a practice routine or training task, a synonym.

clue.text: It's grand to issue handouts

indicators.note: to issue means the word handouts comes out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Giving out handouts is a splendid thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like an adjective meaning splendid, but it is slang for a sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is slang for a sum of a thousand pounds or dollars.

clue.text: Eagerness to reach a U.s. — city may cry about it later

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is a US city

indicators.note: about means the word cry goes around the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Keenness to get to an American city might bring tears afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'later' only fixes the order, putting the crying part last. 'reach' and 'may' are link words in a deliberately chatty surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is brisk readiness or keenness, a synonym.

clue.text: Warning! Try or yield

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout to warn people of a ball in flight
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: A warning: make an attempt or give in.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is shouted on a golf course to warn those ahead of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to give it up or relinquish it, a sense of yield.

clue.text: Constituent at cross-purposes

parts.note: a voter in a constituency marks a cross on a ballot paper, so marking crosses is the purpose of such a person

explanation.surface: A member of the electorate is in disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at cross-purposes' suggests misunderstanding, but it points to the X a voter puts on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is a voter in an MP's constituency, one who chooses a representative.

clue.text: Onslaughts at brad's?

parts.note: brads are small thin nails, so tacks

explanation.surface: Assaults on a person called Brad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brad' looks like a name, but brads are small nails.
explanation.definitionFit: Onslaughts are fierce assaults, a synonym.

clue.text: To flying passengers it may advertise dying

parts.note: to air an idea is to make it public, to advertise it
a terminal illness is one from which the patient is dying

explanation.surface: Something tells air travellers it may announce a death.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the building is a destination to flying passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: An airport building where flights depart and arrive serves as the base for people travelling by plane.

clue.text: Possibly Chippendale may convene

parts.note: a Chippendale is a style of seat, and also one of a troupe of male dancers, so a human seat that calls a meeting

explanation.surface: Perhaps a member of a male dance troupe might call a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Chippendale is a classic furniture maker's style of seat, and the Chippendales are also a male dance troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: The person presiding over a committee calls and runs its meetings.

clue.text: Can hold Muscovite in a friendly way

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining an adjective, read as 'being in a friendly way'

indicators.note: hold means the word for can keeps the mineral inside it

parts.note: if you can do something you are able
muscovite is a common form of the mineral mica

explanation.surface: A tin contains a Russian, all very cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscovite' looks like a person from Moscow, but it is a type of the mineral mica.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable describes relations that are cordial and peaceable, a synonym.

clue.text: Act firm at being a traitor

parts.note: a turn is an act or performance on stage
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company behaves solidly while being treacherous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' and 'firm' read as 'behave steadfastly', but they are a stage turn and a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who switches sides, a betrayer.

clue.text: One at the peak of his ambition

definitions.text: One at the peak of his ambition

parts.words: One at the peak of his ambition
parts.note: the peak is taken literally: a summit, which is what a climber aims to reach

explanation.surface: Someone who has achieved the height of their career goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peak' suggests career success, but read literally it is a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber of high summits aims to stand at the top of a peak.

clue.text: Start to complain and return caravan from U.s.

annotationWithheld.why: Start to complain and return caravan from U.s. (7): T (start to) + RAIL (complain) gives TRAIL, but no clue word gives the closing ER; 'and return' supplies no letters by any reading
annotationWithheld.clue: Start to complain and return caravan from U.s.

clue.text: Draw back from retirement

explanation.surface: Withdrawing from life after leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw back is to withdraw, as an army does; a retirement is a quiet place of seclusion, a hideaway.

clue.text: Cry at church producing illicit whisky

parts.note: a hoot is a cry, as an owl gives

explanation.surface: Shouting in church brings out bootleg spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang for illegally distilled or poor-quality spirits.

clue.text: One taking excessive interest in making advances

definitions.text: One taking excessive interest in making advances

parts.words: One taking excessive interest in making advances
parts.note: interest and advances are read in their money senses: a lender charging an extortionate rate on loans

explanation.surface: Someone who is too keen on making romantic approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excessive interest' and 'advances' suggest an amorous pest, but they are loan terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender who charges exorbitant rates on loans.

clue.text: Do look out for a hollow

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them
cave, Latin for beware, was the schoolboy's cry of look out

explanation.surface: Keep watch for a hole in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (pronounced 'kay-vee') was British public-school slang for 'watch out', from Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A concave surface curves inward like a dish, a hollow shape.

clue.text: A word is taking on gestures

parts.note: mot is French for word, as in bon mot

indicators.note: taking means the word is holds the next word inside it

explanation.surface: Someone says a word is adopting body language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A word' suggests a promise or saying, but the French mot is meant; 'taking' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Motions are movements of the hands or body made to signal, a synonym.

clue.text: It's put up to keep cats and dogs off

definitions.text: It's put up to keep cats and dogs off

parts.words: It's put up to keep cats and dogs off
parts.note: it rains cats and dogs in a downpour, so the thing raised overhead keeps the rain off

explanation.surface: A fence or barrier erected to keep pets away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cats and dogs' suggests pets, but it is heavy rain. BROLLY is British slang for an umbrella.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella is opened overhead to shield a person from rain.

clue.text: Progenitor aggravating enactors

indicators.note: aggravating means the word enactors is stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A forebear who annoys people acting out a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A progenitor is a forebear from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Was wrong to blackmail

parts.note: ex means former, what was once
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone did wrong by extorting money.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to obtain money by threats, the essence of blackmail.

clue.text: A known quarrel maker of old

definitions.text: A known quarrel maker of old

parts.words: A known quarrel maker of old
parts.note: a quarrel is a square-headed crossbow bolt, so this is a historical craftsman making missiles rather than a troublemaker

explanation.surface: Someone long famous for starting arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' suggests an argument, but it is a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A fletcher made arrows and bolts in medieval times.
